hiro_takara.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Transcribed from the shop's own お品書き page (tax included); the site's most recent price-revision notice is dated 2022-08 and 2026 diners still report these bands.

items.note: The lunch flagship: assorted seafood fried in wheat-flour batter, piled on rice. The same bowl is ¥2,000 in the evening. Red-miso soup and pickles come with it; +¥100 for a large rice.
Straight prawn tempura on rice — the safe order if you don't want surprises. ¥2,000 in the evening.
Kakiage is a patty of tiny local Seto Inland Sea shrimp bound in batter and fried whole — crunchier and sweeter than single prawns. ¥2,400 in the evening.
Hiroshima's saltwater conger, battered and fried rather than grilled with tare — a different dish from Miyajima's anago-meshi. ¥2,800 in the evening.
Hiroshima oysters in tempura batter, marked 季節限定・数量限定 — winter only and in limited numbers. A July 2026 diner was told the oyster season had finished. ¥2,400 in the evening.
Freshwater eel grilled and lacquered with sweet tare. The shop is as well known locally for eel as for tempura.

items.en: Grilled eel in a lacquer box, larger portion
items.note: The full-dress version — eel laid edge to edge over rice in a lacquered box. ¥3,500 in the evening; an August 2026 diner reports melon served with it.
Tempura on its own plate with rice, red-miso soup and pickles, instead of piled onto the bowl. Evening only.
The drinking order — tempura alone, without rice, soup or pickles. Diners describe thin, light batter served piece by piece.

items.en: Pufferfish tasting course, reserve by the previous day
items.section: おまかせコース 17:00–22:00 / Chef's course
items.note: Nine courses: appetiser, sashimi, a simmered dish, a grilled dish, tempura, rice, pickles, soup and fruit. Winter-weighted — the shop notes the size of the shirako (milt) changes with the season.

items.en: Tempura dipping broth, served on the side
items.note: Served in a separate cup rather than poured over, which is why regulars praise the crispness here. It is dashi plus wheat-based soy and mirin. Plain salt, 抹茶塩 matcha salt and 柚子塩 yuzu salt are also set out — those are wheat-free, though the batter itself is not.

items.en: Red-miso soup, included with the sets
items.note: Comes with everything except the tempura platter. Built on bonito dashi, so not vegan; red miso is usually soy-only but can be barley-blended.
Plain steamed white rice, so gluten-free and vegan in itself. Offered on everything except the tempura platter.

items.section: ドリンクメニュー / Drinks
items.note: ¥500 for 1 gō (180 ml), ¥820 for 2 gō. Kamotsuru is the celebrated Saijō brewery just east of Hiroshima; sake is brewed from rice and koji alone.

items.ja: 冷酒 加茂鶴ゴールド 300ml
items.en: Kamotsuru Gold chilled sake, 300 ml bottle
items.section: ドリンクメニュー / Drinks
items.note: The daiginjo bottling with gold leaf floating in it — what Japanese drinkers order as a treat. Rice-based, no wheat.

items.ja: 瓶ビール キリン 中瓶
items.section: ドリンクメニュー / Drinks
items.note: Barley malt — beer is never gluten-free. Asahi is stocked at the same price.

items.en: Barley or sweet-potato shochu by the glass
items.section: ドリンクメニュー / Drinks
items.note: ¥400 each, served mizuwari (cut with water), oyuwari (hot water) or on the rocks. The 芋 sweet-potato one is wheat-free; the 麦 is distilled from barley, which most authorities treat as safe but the cautious avoid.

items.ja: 焼酎 宝 麦・芋（キープ）
items.section: ドリンクメニュー / Drinks
items.note: You buy the bottle, drink some, and the shop stores the rest under your name for next time — a normal Japanese custom. 黒霧島, a well-known sweet-potato brand, is ¥3,080 on the same terms.

items.ja: お持ち帰り うな重
items.section: お持ち帰りメニュー / Takeaway
items.note: Takeaway runs ¥300 above the eat-in box. Plain grilled eel with no rice (うなぎ蒲焼) is ¥3,000.

hiro_bakery_roti.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Burger and sandwich prices are read off the shop's own handwritten price cards photographed 2025-04 (the takeaway figure; eat-in is a few yen more). The remaining items and prices come from dated 2024–2026 first-hand reports. A bakery counter changes daily — this is what is usually there, not a fixed list.

items.en: Chicken nanban sandwich — fried chicken in sweet vinegar with tartare sauce
items.section: バーガー・サンド / Burgers & sandwiches
items.note: The shop's card says the tartare is made with free-range egg and black vinegar, on a thick slab of chicken with shredded cabbage. The signature item — one regular has bought it on 84 separate visits. ¥396 eat-in.

items.section: バーガー・サンド / Burgers & sandwiches
items.note: The card reads 'pork chicken cheese' and おろしダレを使い和風に仕上げました — dressed with grated-daikon soy rather than ketchup, with lettuce, mizuna and cheese. A teriyaki version also appears.

items.ja: ささみチーズフライバーガー
items.section: バーガー・サンド / Burgers & sandwiches
items.note: Chicken tenderloin wrapped round Tokachi cheese, crumbed and fried. ¥330 eat-in.

items.section: バーガー・サンド / Burgers & sandwiches
items.note: Karaage tossed in black vinegar, laid in a long roll. ¥330 eat-in. Karaage is dusted in wheat flour or potato starch and comes out of a shared fryer.

items.section: バーガー・サンド / Burgers & sandwiches
items.note: Minced-prawn patty in panko, in a bun. The last digit of the price was cut off in the photograph so it is left blank rather than guessed — its neighbours run ¥248–388.

items.en: Bacon, lettuce and tomato baguette sandwich
items.section: バーガー・サンド / Burgers & sandwiches
items.note: Thick smoky bacon with lettuce and tomato in a soft French roll. A BLTドッグ built in a hot-dog bun (about ¥350) turns up too.

items.en: Ham, onion and cucumber sandwich with cultured butter
items.section: バーガー・サンド / Burgers & sandwiches
items.note: The card lists 玉ネギ・きゅうり・ロースハム with 発酵バター — a plain, old-fashioned deli sandwich. ¥297 eat-in.

items.section: バーガー・サンド / Burgers & sandwiches
items.note: Cheddar, ham, thick-cut cucumber and lettuce in the shop's soft French bread; a 2025-11 buyer found it faintly sweet from the sauce. Price as quoted, before tax.

items.section: バーガー・サンド / Burgers & sandwiches
items.note: Panko-crumbed pork in soft white bread with wheat-based tonkatsu sauce — the classic Japanese sandwich, made in-house and cheap.

items.section: バーガー・サンド / Burgers & sandwiches
items.note: Crustless white bread packed with mashed egg and mayonnaise; generous for the money.

Curry bread here is baked rather than fried, which disappoints people expecting the crunchy kind. A 2024 report priced the then-fried version at ¥209 eat-in; the recipe has since changed, so no price is quoted.

items.ja: カレキャベドッグ（キャベツカレー）
items.en: Retro hot dog under cabbage curry sauce
items.note: A curiosity worth ordering: a sausage roll with cabbage-studded curry sauce poured over, a retro Osaka style nearly extinct elsewhere. Roti puts the curry on top rather than the cabbage underneath.
Russian-derived fried bun with a strongly seasoned meat-and-vegetable filling; reported still crisp hours after frying.

items.ja: 北海道ビーフコロッケ／コロッケバーガー
items.en: Beef croquette, loose or in a bun
items.note: Potato-and-beef croquette in panko, sold on its own and also stuffed into a roll. The recipe was relabelled 北海道ビーフコロッケ around 2025 and regulars preferred the older one.
A whole frankfurter baked into a split roll — the staple of every Japanese neighbourhood bakery.
A very soft koppepan roll with sweet cheddar sauce on top, not inside — the cheapest thing in the shop. Price as quoted, before tax.
A shop invention regulars order by name alongside the chicken nanban; not a standard Japanese bakery item, so point at it if you want to know what's inside.
Another house name; an 84-visit regular calls it simple and outstanding.

items.ja: ベーグル（ブルーベリー）
items.note: Chewy and only lightly sweet, with real blueberry tartness. Bagels normally contain no egg or dairy, but this shop publishes no ingredient list.

items.ja: デニッシュ（鹿児島さつまいも・熊本和栗）
items.en: Seasonal Danish pastries — Kagoshima sweet potato, Kumamoto chestnut
items.note: Danishes named for the region the filling comes from; さつまクルミ (sweet potato and walnut) rotates through the same shelf. Butter pastry, so not vegan.
Crisp outside, soft within. A 2026-02 visitor also singles out the many kiri cream-cheese pastries on the same table — cheese breads are a house strength.

Kilimanjaro-blend beans, ¥150 from the machine beside the eight-seat eat-in corner, which opens early. Black coffee carries no wheat or animal content. A carton café au lait 'made to go with bread' and a coffee milk sit in the fridge by the till.

hiro_teppanyaki_x_fuchuyaki_a.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Transcribed from the shop's own handwritten cards photographed 2026-07 (the yellow okonomiyaki card headed 鉄板焼×府中焼 あっちゃん, plus the 幸せメニュー / じゅうじゅうメニュー side card). An older pink card still in circulation in 2026-06 priced 牛スジしょうが焼き at ¥1,600 and carried two items the yellow card has dropped.

items.en: The standard Hiroshima okonomiyaki — pork, egg and noodles
items.section: お好み焼（そば or うどん）/ Okonomiyaki
items.note: Start here if you have never eaten Hiroshima-style. It is built in layers on the griddle, not stirred: a thin wheat crêpe, a mountain of shredded cabbage, bean sprouts, pork belly, then a nest of fried noodles and an egg cracked over the lot, flipped and painted with sweet-brown okonomi sauce. Choose そば (springy yellow wheat noodles) or うどん (fat, softer). Every layer that matters is wheat — the crêpe, the noodles and the sauce — so there is no way to make it gluten-free.

items.en: Same okonomiyaki with the noodles left out
items.section: お好み焼（そば or うどん）/ Okonomiyaki
items.note: Noodle-free, so it eats lighter and more of the cabbage comes through. Still not gluten-free: the batter crêpe and the okonomi sauce are both wheat.

items.ja: あっちゃんスペシャル
items.en: House special — pork, shiso, raw squid and spring onion
items.section: お好み焼（そば or うどん）/ Okonomiyaki
items.note: The card lists 豚・大葉・生イカ・ネギかけ: pork belly, whole shiso (perilla) leaves, fresh squid, and a heavy scatter of raw spring onion over the top. 大葉 gives it a clean, minty lift that cuts the sauce.

items.en: Deluxe — pork, shiso, squid, cheese and torched onion-mayo
items.section: お好み焼（そば or うどん）/ Okonomiyaki
items.note: The biggest thing on the card: 豚・大葉・生イカ・チーズ・炙りネギマヨ. 炙りネギマヨ means spring onion and mayonnaise blowtorched on top until it blisters.

items.ja: あっちゃんもっちーず
items.section: お好み焼（そば or うどん）/ Okonomiyaki
items.note: A pun on もち (rice cake) and チーズ (cheese). Slices of mochi melt to a stretchy layer against the cheese; イカ天 is a flat sheet of squid tempura that goes soft inside and adds a savoury crunch.

items.ja: 刺激的なあっちゃん焼き
items.en: The fiery one — house extra-hot sauce, pork, kimchi
items.section: お好み焼（そば or うどん）/ Okonomiyaki
items.note: 特製激辛ソース (house super-spicy sauce), pork, kimchi and 辛ねぎ旨すきだれ — a sweet-savoury chilli-onion dressing. 刺激的 means 'stimulating'; take it at its word.

items.en: Spicy cod roe with torched cheese
items.section: お好み焼（そば or うどん）/ Okonomiyaki
items.note: 明太子 is chilli-cured pollock roe — salty, faintly hot, granular. Here it goes on with cheese and torched onion-mayo; the 2026 card notes shiso is included too.

items.section: お好み焼（そば or うどん）/ Okonomiyaki
items.note: 牛スジ is beef tendon stewed until gelatinous — rich and sticky rather than chewy — with spring onion and 紅しょうが, the scarlet pickled ginger. The older pink card prices this one at ¥1,600, so expect either.

items.en: Seafood version — raw squid, raw prawn, pork and shiso
items.section: お好み焼（そば or うどん）/ Okonomiyaki
items.note: 生イカ・生エビ・豚・大葉, and for ¥500 more they add two Hiroshima oysters (カキ2コ) — the local upgrade worth taking in winter.

items.ja: あっちゃんコーンチーズ
items.section: お好み焼（そば or うどん）/ Okonomiyaki
items.note: The mildest thing on the card and the one children order. Sweetcorn against melted cheese; no chilli, no seafood.

Five price bands on the card. ¥150: 目玉焼き fried egg, 野菜ダブル double vegetables, 大葉 shiso. ¥250: ネギかけ spring-onion blanket, もち rice cake, 麺ダブル double noodles. ¥280: ガーリックチップ, とろとろ玉子 soft-set egg. ¥300: こがしマヨ scorched mayo, 明太子 cod roe, コーン, 豚バラ pork belly, イカ天 squid tempura, 生イカ, キムチ, 生エビ. ¥350: 牛スジ beef tendon, チーズ, 炙りネギマヨ, 辛ねぎ旨すきだれ, こぼれネギ. The base pancake is wheat regardless of what you add.

items.en: Salted green soybeans in the pod
items.section: あっちゃん幸せメニュー / Small plates
items.note: Boiled and salted soybeans — no wheat and no animal product, the one dependable order here for either diet, though it shares a kitchen with a griddle covered in wheat sauce.

items.section: あっちゃん幸せメニュー / Small plates
items.note: Torn raw cabbage tossed with a salt-and-oil dressing — the Japanese izakaya palate-cleaner, eaten between mouthfuls of the rich griddle food. The dressing composition is not posted.

items.section: あっちゃん幸せメニュー / Small plates
items.note: Served as a side, also available as a ¥300 topping. Japanese-market kimchi commonly contains fish sauce or salted shrimp, and some brands use wheat-based seasoning.

items.section: あっちゃん幸せメニュー / Small plates
items.note: Mashed-but-lumpy potato with cucumber, carrot and ham in mayonnaise — sweeter and softer than the Western version. Egg-based mayonnaise rules it out for vegans.

items.section: じゅうじゅうメニュー / From the griddle
items.note: げそ is the tentacle end of the squid — chewier and more strongly flavoured than the body. Seared hard on the teppan; the seasoning is soy-based.

items.section: じゅうじゅうメニュー / From the griddle
items.note: せせり is the small strip of muscle from a chicken's neck — one of the juiciest, springiest cuts on the bird, and a yakitori-counter favourite. Soy-based seasoning.

items.section: じゅうじゅうメニュー / From the griddle
items.note: こうね is a Hiroshima word for the fatty cut from the brisket/chuck of the cow — it renders on the griddle to something between bacon and butter. A genuinely local order most visitors never see. Soy-based seasoning.

items.section: じゅうじゅうメニュー / From the griddle
items.note: Hiroshima oysters wrapped in foil with butter and steamed on the teppan, so they poach in their own liquor. Usually finished with soy or a ponzu that is also wheat-based.

hiro_yamamura_chaya.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Transcribed from the shop's own numbered bilingual card photographed 2026-03 and confirmed unchanged 2026-05; all prices tax-included. On both photos items 5 (牡蠣うどん ¥770), 10 (牡蠣丼 ¥880) and 18 are taped over — the oyster dishes are not currently being served, so do not count on them.

items.note: The cheapest thing on the island's menus and a decent shelter from the rain. Thick wheat noodles in a dashi-and-soy broth — bonito dashi and wheat soy, so neither gluten-free nor vegan.
The same bowl with an egg dropped in to set softly in the hot broth.
Thin slices of beef simmered in sweet soy laid over the noodles — the most substantial of the udon.
かやく means the mixed garnish — typically kamaboko fish cake, egg, vegetables and whatever the kitchen has. The card translates it as 'with some kinds of ingredients'.

items.en: Grilled conger eel over rice, with clear soup
items.note: Miyajima's signature dish and by far the most expensive thing here. Saltwater conger (anago, not the freshwater unagi) is split, grilled and lacquered with a sweet tare; the rice underneath is cooked in eel broth. The tare is made with wheat-based soy sauce, which is what rules it out for coeliacs — the eel itself is fine.

items.en: Beef and onion with scrambled egg over rice
items.note: Beef and onion simmered in sweet soy and bound with loosely scrambled egg. Wheat soy in the broth.
'Parent-and-child' — chicken and egg in the same bowl, simmered together in dashi and sweet soy. Comfort food; the soy is wheat-based.
The oyako-don with the chicken left out — onion and egg only, in the same dashi-soy broth.

items.en: Stir-fried noodles with vegetables and pork
items.note: Wheat noodles griddled with cabbage and pork in a sweet-brown fruit-and-soy sauce. Wheat in both the noodles and the sauce.

items.en: Fried rice with beef, egg and vegetables
items.note: Japanese fried rice. The rice is fine in itself but it is finished with a splash of soy sauce, which is wheat-based.
Rice fried with chicken and vegetables in tomato ketchup, a Japanese-Western nursery dish. Ketchup is usually wheat-free but many kitchens add a splash of soy or a bouillon cube.

items.en: Ketchup rice wrapped in a plain omelette
items.note: The chicken rice above, sealed inside a thin omelette — the definitive Japanese comfort dish. Egg rules it out for vegans; the ketchup and any added seasoning are the wheat question.
Mild, thick, faintly sweet Japanese curry — a different animal from Indian curry. Japanese curry roux is thickened with a wheat-flour roux, so this is never gluten-free.

A hand-pressed rice ball, usually with a filling and a wrap of nori. The rice and nori are fine; the filling is the unknown — pickled plum is safe, tuna-mayo and salmon are not vegan, and 昆布 kelp is often simmered in soy.
Plain steamed white rice with nothing on it — genuinely gluten-free and vegan, and the fallback if nothing else works. Ask them not to season it and watch the shared scoop.

The card calls it 'Japanese pot-au-feu' and that is fair: daikon, egg, konnyaku and fish cakes stewed for hours in a soy-dashi broth. Winter food. The broth is bonito dashi and wheat soy, and most fish cakes contain wheat starch.

items.en: Hot sweet red-bean soup with grilled mochi
items.note: Whole azuki beans boiled to a thick sweet soup with a piece of grilled rice cake floating in it — the classic Japanese teahouse sweet, and the reason places like this call themselves 茶屋. Azuki, sugar and rice only, though nothing here is prepared in a wheat-free kitchen.
Thick, cloudy and sweet without any sugar added — rice fermented with koji mould. Served hot; the version made from rice koji is non-alcoholic, the one from sake lees is not, so ask if it matters.
Ordinary drip coffee. Black it contains nothing problematic; milk is dairy.

items.ja: 缶ビール（キリン・アサヒ）
items.note: Cans rather than draught. Barley malt, so never gluten-free.
The single-serve tumbler of sake sold with a foil lid — unglamorous and completely normal. Brewed from rice and koji only.
Bottled soft drinks ¥160, water ¥130 — the cheapest cold drink you will find on the Momijidani side of the island.

hiro_karada_ni_yasashii_sosak.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Taken from the shop's own MENU pages, all tax-included. AGRI publishes no allergen sheet, and the おばんざい change daily — the vegan and gluten notes below say what is normally true of these dishes, not what the shop has certified.

items.en: Nine small home-style dishes with soup and brown rice
items.note: The shop's own number-one seller. おばんざい is the Kyoto-derived word for everyday home cooking served in many small dishes — here nine of them, using more than twenty different ingredients, with soup and the house brown rice. Vegetable-heavy but not vegetarian; the individual dishes are seasoned with soy sauce and dashi and change daily, so ask on the day.

items.en: Low-salt lunch plate, under 2 g of salt
items.note: A five-dish obanzai plate plus a main, soup and brown rice, built to stay under 2 g of sodium — an unusual thing to find on a restaurant menu and the shop's stated speciality (they also sell a low-salt recipe book, ¥2,020). Low salt does not mean no soy sauce.

items.ja: 牛ロースのハンバーグランチ（和風／洋風）
items.en: Beef sirloin hamburg steak lunch, Japanese or Western sauce
items.note: A hand-chopped patty made from steak-grade sirloin rather than trimmings, with soup and brown rice; you pick 和風 (soy-and-daikon) or 洋風 (tomato) sauce. Japanese hamburg is normally bound with panko, and both sauces are wheat-based.

items.ja: 石見ポークのキーマカレーランチ
items.romaji: Iwami Pōku no Kīma Karē Ranchi
items.en: Minced Iwami pork keema curry with a croquette and brown rice
items.note: Keema is dry minced-meat curry rather than the thick brown Japanese kind; Iwami pork comes from neighbouring Shimane. Served with an AGRI croquette and brown rice, free large portion. The croquette is panko-crumbed and Japanese curry is usually thickened with wheat flour.

items.ja: AGRIランチ〜ゆったりランチコース〜
items.en: Sit-down lunch course, six courses with coffee
items.note: Starter, a five-dish obanzai selection, a main, soup, brown rice, dessert and a coffee or tea afterwards. The unhurried option if you have an afternoon.

items.ja: ドリンクセットメニュー
items.note: Coffee, café au lait, iced tea, Ceylon tea, 100% juice (orange, grapefruit, apple, pineapple, mango), dry or ordinary ginger ale, Calpis, oolong tea or soy milk. Black coffee, tea, juice and soy milk are wheat-free; Calpis and café au lait are dairy.

items.en: Dessert and a drink added to lunch
items.note: Dessert plus an after-drink, available to anyone who has ordered a lunch.

items.ja: 宴会ランチ（ご予約限定・飲み放題付）
items.en: Daytime party lunch with free-flow drinks, booking only
items.note: A daytime version of the Japanese 宴会 — set food with unlimited drinks, during lunch hours, reservation required.

items.en: Evening set — eight small dishes, croquette, soup, brown rice, dessert
items.note: The shop's recommended first visit in the evening: eight of the day's obanzai, an お好み焼き風コロッケ (a croquette flavoured like okonomiyaki), vegetable soup, brown rice and a small dessert, across more than twenty ingredients. The croquette is crumbed in panko and carries okonomi sauce, both wheat.

items.ja: 減塩ディナー 〜塩分2g以下〜
items.en: Low-salt dinner, under 2 g of salt
items.note: Starter, pork roasted with mustard, 'circulation' soup, brown rice and dessert, all inside a 2 g sodium budget.
The entry-level omakase — you eat what the kitchen has decided is good that day. A ¥4,400 step up adds a charcoal-grilled domestic sirloin.

items.ja: 料理おまかせコース 4400円
items.en: Chef's choice course with grilled sirloin
items.note: Fresh vegetable salad, a five-dish obanzai selection, a fish dish, charcoal-grilled domestic beef sirloin, brown rice and a small dessert. Add ¥2,000 to make the drinks free-flow.
The top food-only course. A separate ¥5,500 banquet plan bundles 120 minutes of free-flow drinks instead.

items.en: House 'beauty' rice — brown, black and white rice with soybeans
items.section: ディナー単品 / À la carte
items.note: The rice that comes with almost every set here, also sold on its own. The shop states the blend as 玄米・黒米・大豆・白米 — brown rice, black rice, soybeans and white rice, chewy and nutty. Note what is absent: no 押麦 or もち麦 barley, which is what usually contaminates Japanese multigrain rice. Confirm with the kitchen all the same.

items.ja: 小松菜とこぶのとろとろのおひたし
items.romaji: Komatsuna to Kobu no Torotoro no Ohitashi
items.en: Blanched mustard spinach with kelp in a silky broth
items.section: ディナー単品 / À la carte
items.note: Ohitashi is greens briefly blanched and steeped in seasoned broth, served cold. Here komatsuna with finely shredded kombu, which turns the liquid slippery. The broth is soy-seasoned (wheat); whether the dashi is kelp-only or bonito is not stated.

items.ja: 鶏肉と砂肝のピリ辛焼き
items.romaji: Toriniku to Sunagimo no Pirikara Yaki
items.en: Chicken and gizzard, grilled with chilli
items.section: ディナー単品 / À la carte
items.note: 砂肝 is the gizzard — crunchy, mineral, cheap and a standard drinking snack. The shop describes it as a yakitori-mood dish; the seasoning is soy-based.

items.ja: かぼちゃとさつまいものグラタン
items.section: ディナー単品 / À la carte
items.note: Japanese kabocha squash and sweet potato baked under cheese with cinnamon — sweeter than a Western gratin and closer to a side than a dessert. Cheese, and a gratin base that is normally a wheat-flour roux.

items.ja: 牛ロースの荒挽きハンバーグ
items.en: Coarse-ground sirloin hamburg steak, à la carte
items.section: ディナー単品 / À la carte
items.note: The lunch hamburg on its own, coarsely ground so it eats like steak, with a house tomato sauce. Panko binder and wheat-based sauce.

items.ja: 本日のおばんざい（テイクアウト）
items.en: Today's obanzai, single dish to take away
items.note: One dish from the day's obanzai counter, boxed. The cheapest way to try what the kitchen actually does; ask what is in it, because the line-up changes daily.
The menu says only 'ask a member of staff'. A ¥700 assortment (デザートの盛り合わせ) is the better-value order for two.
Described as a palate cleanser to finish on. Dairy.

items.ja: 歓送迎会プラン C【150分飲み放題・料理10品】
items.en: Welcome-and-farewell party plan — ten dishes, 150 minutes free-flow
items.note: Worth reading for what it reveals about the kitchen's range: burrata and seafood salad, five obanzai, Spanish mackerel in cream, sirloin steak, 穴子めし conger-eel rice and dessert, with 70-plus drinks free-flow. Private hire from 10 people, up to 24.

hiro_kura_vitto.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. The hotel's own page describes the bar but posts no priced list, so every price below comes from a dated first-hand visit between 2021 and 2026 and each item says which year. Treat the older figures as indicative only. The tapas line-up is explicitly 日替わり — it changes every day.

items.en: Tapas of the day, small plates
items.note: The reason to come in during the day: the Hotel Miyajima Villa kitchen sends out around six small plates, each ¥300, and the list changes daily. Line-ups reported include roast beef, quiche of the day, green salad, prosciutto with persimmon, oyster gratin, pork-and-turnip pot-au-feu, and cold-poached salmon in ravigote. Go early — one visitor found five of six sold out by late afternoon. (Price reported 2022 and still described as ¥300 tapas in later coverage.)

items.ja: 広島牡蠣のマルゲリータピザ
items.en: Margherita pizza loaded with Hiroshima oysters
items.note: The bar's signature and the thing the hotel advertises — a whole margherita with Hiroshima oysters on it, big enough to share. Wheat base and mozzarella. (Price reported 2022.)
The oyster-free version, ordered by a March 2026 diner who rated the food highly. No price was published.

Spanish-style: oysters poached in olive oil with garlic and chilli, served bubbling, with bread to mop it. The oil and oysters are wheat-free — the bread that comes with it is not. Ordered March 2026; no price published.

Hiroshima's other way with oysters — crumbed in panko and fried, eaten with tartare or a wheat-based tonkatsu sauce. Panko is wheat. (Price reported 2022; a 2022 lunchtime visitor ate them with a glass of draught.)

Marinated fried chicken. One 2022 reviewer thought it tasted like a bought-in product and said so bluntly — order the tapas or the pizza instead. Karaage marinade is soy-based and the coating is wheat flour or starch.
A single daily pasta at a serious 330 g portion; the version reported in 2022 was beef tendon and aubergine in tomato sauce. Wheat pasta.
An odd thing to find in a hotel bar, but a March 2026 diner ordered it alongside the pizza and rated the cooking highly. Fried rice is normally finished with soy sauce.

items.en: Bread from the hotel's own bakery, eaten in
items.note: A nice trick: buy a loaf or a roll at 島旨PAN, the hotel's ground-floor bakery, and you are allowed to eat it here with a drink rather than on a bench with the deer.

items.ja: ハッピーアワー各種ドリンク
items.note: Reported February 2026: between 14:00 and 17:00 draught beer, whisky, wine, sake and cocktails are all ¥500. Given Miyajima's prices and the shortage of anywhere to sit down indoors, this is the best-value hour on the island. Beer is not gluten-free; sake, wine and most spirits are.

items.en: Gin and tonic made with local Sakurao gin
items.note: Sakurao Distillery is in Hatsukaichi, the mainland town Miyajima belongs to, and its gin uses botanicals from the island — including ハマゴウ, the purple beach vitex that grows on Miyajima's shoreline. Add ¥100 to lengthen it with soda. Gin and tonic are wheat-free. (Price reported 2022.)
Three or so of the distillery's gins side by side — a 2021 drinker called ¥900 cheap for what it is. (Price reported 2021.)
Hiroshima is one of Japan's three great sake prefectures, and this is the easiest place on the island to taste several. Ordered March 2026, no price published. Sake is rice and koji only.

items.ja: 桜尾ジン ホワイトハーブス
items.en: Sakurao Gin White Herbs, by the glass
items.note: A limited Sakurao bottling brought back by popular demand; floral and delicate. Seen on a 2024 promotional card and confirmed by a 2024 drinker at ¥880 — a limited run, so it may be gone.

items.ja: ミモザ（ノンアルコール）
items.note: 0% ABV, made with juice from mikan grown at a single Hatsukaichi orchard and non-alcoholic sparkling wine — deep orange and properly citrus-heavy. Seen on a 2024 limited-run card, so check it is still on.
The bar opens at 09:00 and serves coffee from the start — useful, because almost nothing else on Miyajima is open that early. Dairy. (Price reported 2022; a fermented tea, あるけっ茶, was the same price.)

items.ja: 宮島はちみつのソフトクリーム
items.note: Soft-serve ice cream drizzled with honey from the island. Reported by a repeat visitor; no price published, and honey rules it out for vegans in any case.

hiro_toriiya.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Transcribed from 鳥居屋's own site, tax-included. Important: walk-in diners eat at お食事処「とりい」 (10:30–16:00, renewed 21 July, no reservations taken) and that is the menu below; the 鳥居屋 building's own dining room takes groups of 15 or more only, on set courses from ¥1,540 to ¥5,280. The shop says it can accommodate food allergies if you tell them in advance, but publishes an ingredient sheet only for the school-trip menu.

items.ja: 宮島膳（穴子飯・カキフライ・季節の酢の物）
items.en: Miyajima set — conger-eel rice, fried oysters and a seasonal vinegared dish
items.note: Both of the island's specialities on one tray, which is exactly what most visitors want. 穴子飯 is grilled saltwater conger over rice cooked in eel broth; カキフライ is Hiroshima oysters crumbed and fried. The eel tare is wheat-based soy and the oyster crumb is panko.

items.en: Fried oyster set with small dish, pickles and soup
items.note: Hiroshima grows the majority of Japan's oysters and this is the everyday way locals eat them — panko-crumbed, fried, with tartare or tonkatsu sauce. Panko and sauce are both wheat.
Four large crumbed prawns with rice, a small dish, pickles and clear soup.
The safe non-seafood order for anyone travelling with someone who won't eat oysters. Panko crumb and a fruit-and-soy tonkatsu sauce, both wheat.
Six pieces of chicken marinated in soy, ginger and garlic, dusted and fried. The cheapest set on the list and the one children order.

items.en: Grilled conger eel in a lacquer box
items.note: Miyajima's signature dish in its full-dress form. Saltwater conger — leaner and more delicate than freshwater unagi — split, grilled over charcoal and lacquered with sweet tare, laid over rice cooked in the bones' broth. The tare is made with wheat soy sauce; there is no way round it.
The set meal's oysters, served on the rice with sauce poured over — cheaper and quicker.
むきみ means shucked meat — the oysters go on unfried, cooked in a sweet-savoury broth with onion and egg, which suits people who find the fried version heavy. The broth is soy-based.

items.en: Pork cutlet simmered with egg over rice
items.note: A fried cutlet re-simmered with onion in dashi and sweet soy, then bound with barely-set egg — one of Japan's great comfort dishes.
'Parent and child' — chicken and egg together in a dashi-and-soy broth. The cheapest full meal on the menu.

items.ja: 穴子飯温うどん・そばセット
items.en: Small conger-eel rice with a bowl of hot udon or soba
items.note: The sensible way to try anago-meshi without committing ¥3,000 — a smaller portion of the eel rice paired with a hot noodle bowl. Both noodle choices are wheat (Japanese soba is normally wheat-blended unless it says 十割).

items.ja: ちりめんご飯温うどん・そばセット
items.en: Baby-whitebait rice with hot udon or soba
items.note: ちりめん (ちりめんじゃこ) is tiny dried sardine fry scattered over rice — a Seto Inland Sea staple, salty and calcium-heavy. The budget version of the set above.
Noodles served in a small iron pot with oysters and vegetables, bubbling when it reaches you — winter food, and the local answer to a cold day on the island.

items.en: Udon baked in its own iron pot
items.note: Udon simmered and served in a lidded clay or iron pot, usually with a prawn tempura, egg, fish cake and mushroom on top.

items.en: Noodles in hot broth with prawn tempura
items.note: A prawn tempura set on top of the noodles, where it slowly softens in the broth — that is intentional.
The cheapest hot dish here. Sweet-simmered beef slices over noodles in dashi broth.

items.ja: 天ざるそば・ざるうどん
items.en: Cold noodles on a bamboo tray with tempura
items.note: Summer eating: chilled noodles served drained on a slatted tray, dipped mouthful by mouthful into cold soy-dashi tsuyu, with tempura alongside. Anago-meshi and chirimen-rice versions of the cold set are ¥2,000 and ¥1,350. Wheat noodles, wheat soy in the dip.

items.en: Hiroshima ramen — pork-bone and soy broth, thin noodles
items.note: Hiroshima's own style: a pork-bone broth darkened and seasoned with soy, lighter than Hakata tonkotsu, with thin straight noodles. Wheat noodles and wheat soy.

items.en: Onomichi ramen — soy broth with pork-back fat, flat noodles
items.note: From the port town along the coast: a clear soy broth built on small dried fish, with lumps of rendered pork back-fat floating on top and flat noodles. Distinctly different from the Hiroshima bowl beside it.
藻塩 is salt made by boiling seawater with seaweed, an ancient Seto Inland Sea method revived on nearby Kamikamagari island — mineral and slightly sweet. The clearest, lightest of the three broths.

items.ja: かきフライカレー（サラダ付）
items.en: Japanese curry with fried oysters and salad
items.note: Thick, mild, faintly sweet Japanese curry with fried oysters on top. The roux is wheat-thickened, on top of the panko.

items.en: Oysters grilled in the shell, six pieces
items.section: 一品料理・おつまみ / Small plates
items.note: Grilled at the shopfront, so you can eat them standing up on Omotesando like everyone else. The oyster and the shell are all there is — but the squeeze of ponzu usually offered contains wheat-based soy, so ask for lemon only. Fried oysters (6 pieces) are ¥1,600 and karaage (6 pieces) ¥1,300.

items.ja: もみじクロワッサン（もみクロ）
items.en: Maple-leaf croissant — a croissant baked in the momiji-manju mould
items.section: お土産・軽食 / Sweets & souvenirs
items.note: Toriiya's own invention and a genuinely new Miyajima snack (they have a trademark application in): croissant dough pressed in the maple-leaf iron used for momiji manju, so it comes out flaky rather than spongy. Six fillings always on: 粒あん chunky red bean, cream, apple, chocolate, cheese, plus one seasonal. Sold hot at the shopfront.

items.ja: もみじまんじゅう（こしあん）8個入
items.en: Maple-leaf cakes with smooth red-bean paste, box of 8
items.section: お土産・軽食 / Sweets & souvenirs
items.note: The island's defining souvenir, invented on Miyajima around 1906 — a maple-leaf-shaped castella sponge with filling. Toriiya bakes its own, using plenty of egg for a fluffy crumb and making the bean paste in-house. 15 pieces ¥2,180; assorted boxes mix koshian, 粒あん chunky bean, 抹茶, cream and chocolate at ¥1,450 for 10. Wheat flour and egg — the sponge is a cake batter, so never gluten-free and never vegan.

items.en: Strawberry shaved ice, shaved from a frozen fruit block
items.section: お土産・軽食 / Sweets & souvenirs
items.note: Not syrup on ice: a column of ice with whole strawberries frozen into it is shaved down, so the fruit is the flavour. April to October only, and their summer best-seller. Condensed milk is offered on top and is dairy — without it the plain ice is fruit and water. No price is posted.
